mainTopic: לולב on שבת today, why לולב but not ערבה is done seven days זכר למקדש, and the source and status of the ערבה מצוה
overview: The גמרא first rules that today, even in ארץ ישראל, the לולב does not override שבת. It reinterprets two sources about bringing לולבים on ערב שבת so that both describe the time of the מקדש. Then אביי asks רבא why we take the לולב all seven days זכר למקדש but not the ערבה. רבא's first answer is rejected. רב זביד then says in רבא's name that לולב is דאורייתא and ערבה is דרבנן. That wording is attacked, because for both אבא שאול and the רבנן the ערבה of the מקדש is more than rabbinic. So it is re-worded: the לולב has a written Torah root even in the גבולין, while the ערבה does not. Next, ריש לקיש rules that blemished כהנים may enter for the ערבה, and רבי יוחנן questions how and by whom the מצוה is done. Finally, the גמרא sorts out רבי יוחנן's conflicting statements on whether the ערבה is from סיני, a יסוד נביאים, or the חכמים' own enactment. The last answer begins with לא קשיא and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even in ארץ ישראל, the לולב does not override שבת today
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים state that even for the people of ארץ ישראל, who know the correct calendar, the לולב does not override שבת nowadays.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: even for them (the people of ארץ ישראל), the לולב does not override שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a ruling: today, nobody takes the לולב on שבת. This includes people in ארץ ישראל, even though they have no doubt about the calendar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason given for not taking the לולב on שבת was that people outside ארץ ישראל don't know which day the month began. One might think people in ארץ ישראל, who do know the date, should still take it. This statement says no. They also don't take it on שבת today.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the Sages) say
For them, meaning the people of ארץ ישראל
Overrides (pushes aside) שבת

phrases.english: They say:
For them (in Eretz Yisrael) also, it does not override Shabbat.
phrases.notes: Even where the date is known, lulav today does not push aside Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לְדִידְהוּ נָמֵי לָא דָּחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about why לולב does not override שבת today.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nowadays, even in ארץ ישראל, the מצוה of לולב does not override שבת.

steps.title: Challenge from the two sources about where the לולבים are brought
steps.stepSummary: If לולב never overrides שבת today, then our old way of resolving two conflicting sources no longer works.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then the two sources are difficult. One source teaches: all the people bring their לולבים to the הר הבית. Another source teaches: they bring them to the בית הכנסת. We used to resolve this by saying one source speaks about when the מקדש stands, and the other speaks about when the מקדש does not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling from Step 1. It brings two sources that seem to contradict each other, along with the standard way of resolving them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources describe people bringing their לולבים on ערב שבת so they can take them on שבת. That means the לולב overrides שבת. We used to explain the 'synagogue' source as referring to the time after the מקדש was destroyed. That explanation means the לולב still overrode שבת even without the מקדש. This clashes with Step 1, which says the לולב does not override שבת today.

keyTerms.meaning: These two (sources)
The Temple Mount
The synagogue
And we resolved (it)
At a time when the Temple is standing

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the contradiction itself, which was already solved. The problem is that the old solution assumed the לולב overrides שבת even after the חורבן. That assumption is what clashes with Step 1.

phrases.english: But then these two (sources) are difficult;
for one source teaches:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעָם מוֹלִיכִין אֶת לוּלְבֵיהֶן לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: All the people bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount,
and another source teaches: to the synagogue,
and we resolved it:
Here, when the Temple is standing,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים.
phrases.english: there, when the Temple is not standing.
phrases.notes: This implies the לולב still overrode שבת after the חורבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא קַשְׁיָא הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of Step 1 using an accepted resolution of two sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the לולב does not override שבת today, even in ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our accepted resolution of the two sources assumes that the 'synagogue' source describes the time after the חורבן, when the לולב still overrode שבת. That contradicts Step 1.

steps.title: Both sources refer to when the מקדש stood: one in the מקדש, one in the outlying towns
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the old resolution. Both sources speak about the time of the מקדש. One describes the מקדש itself, and the other describes the rest of the country.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both sources speak about when the מקדש is standing, and there is no difficulty. This source is about the מקדש, and that source is about the outlying areas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by giving a new way to resolve the two sources. This new way does not require the לולב to override שבת after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, people brought their לולבים to הר הבית. In the rest of ארץ ישראל, they brought them to the local synagogue. Both describe the time of the מקדש, so neither source proves that the לולב overrides שבת today. The ruling of Step 1 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one (both sources)
And it is not difficult
Outlying areas (outside the מקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: Today the לולב does not override שבת anywhere. Both sources about bringing לולבים on ערב שבת describe the time of the מקדש: one in the מקדש, one in the גבולין.

phrases.english: No, both this and that
refer to when the Temple is standing,
and it is not difficult:
here, in the Temple,
there, in the outlying areas.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 2 by replacing the old resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the sources: changing which situation the second source describes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'synagogue' source describes the time after the חורבן, so the לולב overrode שבת even then.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sources describe the time of the מקדש: one in the מקדש, one in the גבולין. Nothing shows the לולב overrides שבת today.

steps.title: אביי asks why לולב is taken seven days but ערבה is not
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבא why we take the לולב all seven days זכר למקדש, but do not take the ערבה all seven days זכר למקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: What is different about the לולב, that we do it seven days in memory of the מקדש? And what is different about the ערבה, that we do not do it seven days in memory of the מקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. אביי asks why two מצוות of the מקדש are treated differently today. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, both the לולב and the ערבה were done all seven days. After the חורבן, the חכמים set up the לולב for seven days everywhere זכר למקדש. Yet the ערבה is done only on one day (הושענא רבה). אביי wants to know the reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different (about this case)?
In memory of the Temple
Willow branch (the מקדש מצוה of the ערבה)
We do / perform

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rava:
What is different about lulav
that we do it seven days in memory of the Temple,
and what is different about the willow

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא עָבְדִינַן לַהּ שִׁבְעָה זֵכֶר לַמִּקְדָּשׁ?
phrases.english: that we do not do it seven days in memory of the Temple?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרָבָא: מַאי שְׁנָא לוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic related to remembering the מקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תקנה of זכר למקדש covers seven days of לולב but not seven days of ערבה.

steps.title: רבא: we already fulfill with the ערבה inside the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a person already takes a ערבה every day, since it is bound together with the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Because a person fulfills his obligation with the ערבה that is in the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a first answer. A separate seven-day ערבה is not needed, because the ערבה bound in the לולב is already taken every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the memory of the מקדש ערבה is already covered. Every day of סוכות we lift a ערבה as part of the four species, so no extra practice is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Since / because
Fulfills his obligation
The willow that is bound with the lulav

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since a person fulfills his obligation
with the willow that is in the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְאָדָם יוֹצֵא יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בָּעֲרָבָה שֶׁבַּלּוּלָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ערבה is already taken daily as part of the לולב bundle, so a separate seven-day ערבה זכר למקדש is not needed.

steps.title: אביי: that ערבה is taken for the לולב מצוה, not for the ערבה מצוה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's answer. The ערבה in the bundle is taken for the מצוה of the four species, not as a separate ערבה מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That one, he does it because of the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's answer. He points out that lifting the ערבה inside the לולב is part of the לולב מצוה, so it cannot also count as the separate ערבה practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה of the מקדש was its own separate מצוה. The ערבה in the bundle is one of the four species. Doing the four-species מצוה does not remind us of the separate מקדש ערבה, so רבא's answer seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that act)
Because of / for the sake of

phrases.english: He said to him:
That is because of the lulav
that he does it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִשּׁוּם לוּלָב הוּא דְּקָא עָבֵיד לַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the ערבה in the לולב covers the ערבה זכר למקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One act done for the four-species מצוה cannot count as the separate ערבה מצוה.

steps.title: Lifting the bundle a second time is not the practice
steps.stepSummary: אביי blocks a possible defense: maybe one lifts the bundle twice, once for each מצוה. He answers that everyday practice shows nobody does this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that he lifts it and then lifts it again, but daily practice shows that we do not do this!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי closes a possible escape route for רבא's answer. Someone might say the bundle is lifted a second time for the ערבה. אביי replies that this is simply not what people do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lifting the bundle twice would make the second lifting count for the ערבה. But the common daily practice is to lift it only once, so this defense fails. רבא's first answer is now fully rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
Lifts
And then again
Everyday actions / common practice

phrases.english: And if you will say

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָא מַגְבַּהּ לַיהּ וַהֲדַר מַגְבַּהּ לַיהּ,
phrases.english: that he lifts it and then lifts it again,
but everyday practice shows
that we do not do so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּקָא מַגְבַּהּ לַיהּ וַהֲדַר מַגְבַּהּ לַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the attack of Step 6 by removing a possible defense.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possible defense that the bundle is lifted twice, once for the ערבה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It does not match actual practice. People lift the לולב only once.

steps.title: רב זביד: לולב is דאורייתא, ערבה is דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד, in the name of רבא, gives a new answer. The לולב is a Torah-level מצוה, so it was extended to seven days. The ערבה is only רבנן, so it was not extended. Steps 9 and 10 challenge this wording, and Step 11 replaces it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: The לולב, which is from the Torah, we do seven days in memory of the מקדש. The ערבה, which is from the רבנן, we do not do seven days in memory of the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new answer is given in רבא's name, replacing the rejected one: לולב is דאורייתא and ערבה is דרבנן. The next steps challenge this wording, and Step 11 gives a corrected version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that the חכמים extended only a Torah-level מצוה, the לולב, to seven days. They did not extend the ערבה, which this version calls simply דרבנן. That is exactly what the next step challenges, since the ערבה of the מקדש may not be rabbinic at all.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
From the Torah
From the Rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: This first wording, 'לולב is דאורייתא, ערבה is דרבנן', does not stand. The גמרא challenges it in Steps 9 and 10 and replaces it in Step 11.
steps.whyThisMatters: Today's practice (לולב every day of סוכות, but ערבה only on הושענא רבה) is explained by the corrected wording in Step 11, not by this first wording, which Steps 9-10 attack.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
Lulav, which is Torah law —
we do it seven days in memory of the Temple,
willow, which is rabbinic —

phrases.aramaic: לָא עָבְדִינַן לַהּ שִׁבְעָה זֵכֶר לַמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: we do not do it seven days in memory of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: לוּלָב דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to אביי's question after the first answer (Step 5) was rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two מצוות by their source: דאורייתא versus דרבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ערבה is not extended because it is already taken inside the לולב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The memorial was extended only to the מצוה with a Torah basis outside the מקדש, which is the לולב, and not to the ערבה, which is only רבנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Not final: this wording is challenged in Steps 9 and 10 and replaced in Step 11 with 'explicit Torah root versus no explicit Torah root, in the גבולין'.

steps.title: Whose view is it? Not אבא שאול, who learns the ערבה from a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that ערבה is only רבנן. According to אבא שאול, the plural ״ערבי נחל״ teaches two Torah-level ערבות, one for the לולב and one for the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did רבא say this? If you say אבא שאול, he says that ״ערבי נחל״ is written in the plural, meaning two: one for the לולב and one for the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier answer that ערבה is only a rabbinic law. It asks which תנא could hold that view. It starts by showing that אבא שאול cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול reads the plural ״ערבי״ as two separate ערבות. One goes in the לולב bundle, and one is for the special ערבה מצוה in the מקדש. So for him, the ערבה of the מקדש comes straight from the Torah, not from the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which opinion does this follow?
If you say (the first option being tested)
A תנא who learns the ערבה from the plural form of the פסוק
'Willows of the brook,' written in the plural in ויקרא כג:מ

steps.confusionAlert: This קשיא directly attacks רב זביד's wording in Step 8, that the ערבה is דרבנן. Step 11 then re-words the answer ('אֶלָּא...') so that it survives this attack.

phrases.english: According to whom?
phrases.notes: According to which opinion is ערבה only rabbinic?

phrases.english: If you say Abba Shaul,
but he said 'willows (plural) of the brook' is written,
meaning two: one for the lulav
and one for the Temple.
phrases.notes: So for אבא שאול the מקדש ערבה is from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַבָּא שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'ערבה is rabbinic' basis of רבא's distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ערבה is only a rabbinic law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For אבא שאול, the plural ״ערבי נחל״ makes the מקדש ערבה a Torah law.

steps.title: Not the רבנן either, since for them ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: The second option also fails. The רבנן hold that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני, as רבי יוחנן taught in the name of רבי נחוניא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the רבנן, they received it as a tradition. As רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי נחוניא of the valley of בית חורתן: the ten saplings, the ערבה, and the water libation are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its attack. Even the רבנן, who do not learn ערבה from a פסוק, hold that it is a tradition from סיני, so it is not merely rabbinic either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני has Torah-level authority even though it is not written in the text. So both sides of the מחלוקת give the ערבה of the מקדש more than rabbinic status, and the claim 'ערבה is דרבנן' collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned it as an oral tradition
A law given orally to משה at סיני, with Torah-level force
The ten saplings: a law about plowing near young trees before שביעית
The water libation on the מזבח during סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement of רבי אסי appears again in Step 14 as the basis for a second challenge.

phrases.english: If according to the Rabbis,
they learned it as a tradition,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: as Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Nechunya of the valley of Beit Chortan:
the ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation
are a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לְרַבָּנַן, הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the 'whose opinion?' attack, closing off the רבנן option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ערבה is only a rabbinic law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the רבנן, ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so it is not rabbinic.

steps.title: Re-wording: the לולב has an explicit Torah source, the ערבה does not
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד, in the name of רבא, re-words the distinction. It is not 'Torah versus rabbinic' but 'explicitly written in the Torah versus not written.' The לולב has a written source everywhere, while the ערבה has no written source, so only the לולב was extended to seven days outside the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב זביד said in the name of רבא: the לולב, which has a basis written in the Torah, we do seven days outside the מקדש זכר למקדש. The ערבה, which has no basis written in the Torah, we do not do seven days outside the מקדש זכר למקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a corrected version of רבא's answer, which avoids the attack of Steps 9 and 10. It replaces Step 8's 'דאורייתא versus דרבנן' wording, which was refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new key word is עיקר, meaning a written root. The לולב has a written פסוק (״ולקחתם לכם ביום הראשון״) that applies even outside the מקדש. The ערבה, even if it is Torah-level as a הלכה למשה מסיני, has no written root, so the חכמים did not extend it outside the מקדש for seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: A root or basis written explicitly in the Torah
Places outside the מקדש
A remembrance of the מקדש
The אמורא who reports רבא's corrected answer

steps.whatToRemember: The לולב is taken all seven days outside the מקדש because it has a written Torah root. The ערבה lacks a written root, so even though it is a הלכה למשה מסיני, it was not extended outside the מקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that ערבה is 'only rabbinic.' The גמרא just showed it is not. The point is only that it lacks a written source in the Torah text.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:

phrases.aramaic: לוּלָב דְּאִית לֵיהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה, —
phrases.english: the lulav, which has a basis in the Torah,
outside the Temple we do it seven days
in remembrance of the Temple;

phrases.aramaic: עֲרָבָה דְּלֵית לַהּ עִיקָּר מִן הַתּוֹרָה —
phrases.english: the willow, which has no basis in the Torah,
outside the Temple we do not do seven days
in remembrance of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'whose opinion?' challenge by re-wording the distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reformulation: 'explicitly written' versus 'not written' instead of 'Torah' versus 'rabbinic'
steps.terutzMaskana: ערבה lacks an explicit written Torah root, so it was not extended to seven days outside the מקדש.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: blemished כהנים may enter between the אולם and the מזבח for the ערבה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that כהנים בעלי מומין may enter the restricted area between the אולם and the מזבח to fulfill the ערבה מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: כהנים with blemishes may enter between the אולם and the מזבח in order to fulfill the מצוה of ערבה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins, still about the ערבה in the מקדש. ריש לקיש gives a ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a blemished כהן may not enter the area between the אולם and the מזבח. Going around the מזבח with the ערבה means passing through that area. ריש לקיש says the ערבה מצוה applies to them too, so they may enter.

keyTerms.meaning: כהנים with physical blemishes
The area between the Entrance Hall and the מזבח, which is restricted
To fulfill an obligation
An אמורא in ארץ ישראל and partner of רבי יוחנן

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Priests with blemishes
may enter between the Entrance Hall and the altar
in order to fulfill the מצוה of the willow.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כֹּהֲנִים בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Related topic: a new ruling about the ערבה in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blemished כהנים may enter between the אולם and the מזבח to perform the ערבה מצוה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks: who said so?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן questions ריש לקיש's ruling with the words 'Who said it?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Who said this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש by asking what the source is for this ruling. This sets up the גמרא's next question about what רבי יוחנן meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מי אמרה' are vague. At first they sound like he doubts the whole ערבה מצוה in the מקדש. The גמרא will explore what he actually doubted.

keyTerms.meaning: Who said it? A challenge demanding a source

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
Who said it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִי אֲמָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling about בעלי מומין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Questions whether there is any source for the ruling.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן himself taught that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised at רבי יוחנן's question. He himself transmitted the teaching that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who said it?! He himself said it! As רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי נחוניא of the valley of בית חורתן: the ten saplings, the ערבה, and the water libation are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's question. How can he ask 'who said it' about the ערבה מצוה when he is the one who taught that it comes from סיני?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same statement quoted in Step 10 is repeated here for a new purpose: to show a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's own words. If the ערבה מצוה is clearly from סיני, his doubt seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: But he himself said it!

phrases.english: 'Who said it'?!
But he himself said it!

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: As Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Nechunya of the valley of Beit Chortan:
the ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation
are a law given to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אֲמָרָהּ?! הָא אִיהוּ אֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's own question from Step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן himself taught that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני, so how can he doubt it?

steps.title: His doubt was about the details: carrying versus standing up, and blemished versus unblemished
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן did not doubt the ערבה מצוה itself. He doubted two details. First, maybe the מצוה is done by standing the ערבה up beside the מזבח rather than carrying it around. Second, maybe only unblemished כהנים may do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, his question was this. Who said the מצוה is done by taking the ערבה? Maybe it is done by standing it upright. Who said it may be done by blemished כהנים? Maybe only by unblemished ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by explaining what רבי יוחנן really meant. He accepted the מצוה but questioned how it is done and who may do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מצוה is only standing the ערבה up, there is no need to walk around the מזבח through the restricted area. Even if it is carried, perhaps only תמימים may do it. Either way, ריש לקיש's permission for בעלי מומין to enter is not proven.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking or carrying the ערבה
Standing the ערבה upright beside the מזבח
כהנים without blemishes
Perhaps

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן agrees that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני. He only questions how it is done (carrying or standing) and by whom (only unblemished כהנים?), and that is why ריש לקיש's ruling is not proven.

phrases.english: Rather: who said it is done by taking?
Perhaps it is done by standing it upright!
Who said it may be done by blemished priests?
Perhaps only by unblemished ones!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מִי אֲמָרָהּ בִּנְטִילָה, דִּלְמָא בִּזְקִיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן doubted the very existence of the ערבה מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: He doubted only how the מצוה is performed and who may perform it.

steps.title: Two אמוראים argue: ordinance or custom of the נביאים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי argue about the ערבה. One says it is a יסוד נביאים and the other says it is a מנהג נביאים. Step 17 shows who holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One said the ערבה is an ordinance set up by the נביאים. The other said the ערבה is just a custom of the נביאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new disagreement about how strong the ערבה מצוה is. It does not say here which אמורא holds which side; Step 17 identifies them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יסוד נביאים is a binding rule that the נביאים (חגי, זכריה, מלאכי) put in place. A מנהג נביאים is only a practice they kept, which others adopted, with no formal obligation. This difference decides how seriously the ערבה must be treated, for example whether a ברכה is said on it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a dispute between אמוראים
A binding ordinance established by the prophets
A custom practiced by the prophets, not a formal obligation
One said... and one said: the views are given without saying who holds which

steps.confusionAlert: Both views agree the ערבה came through the נביאים. The argument is only about whether it is a binding rule or just a custom.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi disagree.
One said: the willow is an ordinance of the prophets,
and one said: the willow is a custom of the prophets.
phrases.notes: A custom is something practiced, not formally required.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, חַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the source and strength of the ערבה מצוה, after the earlier steps about ערבה in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת whether ערבה is a יסוד נביאים (binding) or a מנהג נביאים (custom).

steps.title: Proving that רבי יוחנן holds it is a prophetic ordinance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from a statement of רבי אבהו, quoting רבי יוחנן, that רבי יוחנן is the one who said יסוד נביאים. The proof is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: We can conclude that רבי יוחנן is the one who said 'ordinance of the נביאים.' This is because רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: 'The ערבה is an ordinance of the נביאים.' Yes, we can conclude this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא figures out who held which view in the previous step. It uses a separate quote from רבי יוחנן and then confirms the conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו quotes רבי יוחנן using the exact phrase 'יסוד נביאים'. So the 'יסוד' view belongs to רבי יוחנן, and the 'מנהג' view belongs to רבי יהושע בן לוי. The final word 'תסתיים' means the גמרא accepts the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Conclude: introduces a proof identifying a view. When repeated at the end, it means the proof is accepted
The אמורא who transmits רבי יוחנן's statement

phrases.english: Conclude that it is Rabbi Yochanan
who said 'an ordinance of the prophets,'

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
'The willow is an ordinance of the prophets.'
Indeed, conclude so.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיַּים דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר יְסוֹד נְבִיאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies who holds each view in the מחלוקת of step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן holds ערבה is a יסוד נביאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו's quote of רבי יוחנן: 'ערבה יסוד נביאים הוא'.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks: didn't רבי יוחנן call it a law from Sinai?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי אבהו. רבי יוחנן himself taught, in the name of רבי נחוניא, that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני. So how could he call it an ordinance of the נביאים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אבהו: Did רבי יוחנן really say that? Didn't רבי יוחנן say, in the name of רבי נחוניא from the valley of בית חורתן: 'The ten saplings, the ערבה, and the water libation are each a הלכה למשה מסיני'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא points out that two statements of רבי יוחנן seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A law from סיני is much older and stronger than a rule made by the later נביאים. If the ערבה goes back to משה, the נביאים could not have been the ones to establish it. So the two quotes of רבי יוחנן clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? This opens a challenge to an attributed statement
A law given orally to משה at Sinai, without a verse
Ten saplings: a rule about plowing near young trees before שביעית
The water libation poured on the מזבח on סוכות

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rabbi Abbahu:
Did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Nechunya of the valley of Beit Chortan:
The ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation
are a law given to Moses at Sinai?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 17 by quoting a conflicting statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds ערבה is a יסוד נביאים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן taught that ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני. A law from Sinai cannot also have been first established by the later נביאים.

steps.title: It was forgotten, and the prophets re-established it
steps.stepSummary: After thinking for a while, רבי אבהו answers. The ערבה really is from סיני, but it was forgotten during גלות בבל, and the נביאים restored it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was stunned for a moment, and then he said: They forgot these laws, and then the נביאים went back and re-established them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו resolves the contradiction by saying that both of רבי יוחנן's statements are true at different points in history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערבה started as a הלכה למשה מסיני. It was forgotten during גלות בבל. The נביאים then 'founded it again', which is why it is also called יסוד נביאים. So 'יסוד' here means re-establishing an old law, not inventing a new one.

keyTerms.meaning: He was astonished for a moment: a phrase borrowed from דניאל ד:טז
They forgot them, and then went back and re-established them

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that a law can be from סיני and also be called a 'founding' of the נביאים. The נביאים restored a law that had been lost; they did not create it.

phrases.english: He was astonished for a moment
phrases.notes: Language from Daniel 4:16. He took time to think before answering.

phrases.english: and said: they forgot them, and then they went back and re-established them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶשְׁתּוֹמַם כְּשָׁעָה חֲדָא וַאֲמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reconciles the two statements by placing them in two historical stages (original law, then restoration).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יסוד נביאים' means the נביאים created the ערבה law, so it cannot be from Sinai.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ערבה is from Sinai. It was forgotten in exile, and the נביאים re-established it, which is why it is called יסוד נביאים.

steps.title: A third statement: רבי יוחנן calls it a rabbinic practice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. רבי יוחנן also said, 'Yours say: it is theirs.' This treats the ערבה as an institution of the חכמים, not from סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: And did רבי יוחנן really say it is from סיני? Didn't רבי יוחנן say: 'Your חכמים (in בבל) say: it is theirs!'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to conflict with calling the ערבה a law from Sinai.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this quote, the ערבה is 'theirs', meaning an enactment of the חכמים. That clashes with the claim that רבי יוחנן holds it is a הלכה למשה מסיני. So even after step 19, רבי יוחנן's statements still do not line up.

keyTerms.meaning: Yours: the חכמי בבל being addressed
It is theirs: an institution of the חכמים

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
'Yours (the Babylonian Sages) say: it is theirs!'
phrases.notes: 'Theirs' means instituted by the Sages, not a law from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 reconciled 'Sinai' with 'נביאים', this step raises a new conflicting statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds ערבה is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן elsewhere calls the ערבה 'theirs', a rabbinic institution. That cannot fit with it being a law from Sinai.

steps.title: Beginning the answer: it is not a contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that the contradiction can be resolved. The actual explanation comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא says the contradiction can be solved, and it is about to explain how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us that both statements of רבי יוחנן will turn out to be correct. Usually this means each one refers to a different case or situation. The details follow right on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult: introduces an answer showing that two sources do not really conflict

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here. The answer itself has not been given yet; it continues in the next part of the דף.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Announces a reconciliation (two statements refer to different cases). The details continue on the next amud.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's statements about the source of ערבה contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pending: the explanation follows on the next amud.
